description_text:
The Talent Acquisition Consultant (Visa and Relocation) delivers high quality end to end services and support to managers particularly in the recruitment of positions where the expected applicant is overseas or interstate.

* **Salary $125K - $140K per annum plus 17% superannuation**
* **Full-time continuing appointment**
* **Macquarie University, Wallumattagal Campus, North Ryde**

***Open the door for global talent – specialist immigration expertise that brings the world's best minds to Macquarie***

Every year, academics, researchers, clinicians and professional staff from around the world choose to build their careers at Macquarie University. Behind each of those arrivals sits a visa pathway to navigate, a nomination to lodge, a family to settle and a compliance obligation to meet. This is where you come in.

As our Visa, Relocation and Global Mobility Specialist, you will be the University's subject matter expert on immigration and mobility. You will advise hiring managers, faculty leadership and candidates on visa options and eligibility, manage the end-to-end visa lifecycle for international academics and researchers, and coordinate relocation arrangements that help new starters and their families settle in quickly. You will also safeguard the University's compliance position, maintaining sponsorship records, monitoring visa expiries and keeping us audit-ready.

Sitting within the Talent Acquisition team in Human Resources, this is a rare specialist role in a complex, highly regulated environment where your advice has visible impact on individual careers, on research programs, and on Macquarie's ability to attract the best talent globally. If you enjoy untangling intricate immigration matters and translating legislation into clear, practical guidance, you will find plenty of scope here.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Head of Talent Acquisition, you will provide specialist, high-level guidance, information, compliance oversight and reporting on immigration and relocation matters to internal stakeholders, current staff, prospective staff and international visitors.

Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Providing expert advice to hiring managers and University leaders on visa and immigration regulations, compliance and reporting
* Assessing visa eligibility, explaining visa subclasses (including 407, 408, 482 and 186) and outlining step-by-step processes for existing staff, prospective employees and visiting academics
* Managing the visa lifecycle for distinguished researchers and postdoctoral fellows, including employer nomination processing and correspondence with government departments
* Applying and upholding the University's immigration policies and procedures, mitigating risk across all cases and escalating any breaches
* Maintaining mandatory sponsorship records, tracking visa expiry dates and work right compliance and ensuring readiness for federal immigration audits
* Acting as the primary contact point between the University, external legal counsel and government departments, and liaising with external agencies to resolve issues as they arise
* Coordinating international and domestic relocation benefits, housing resources and onboarding logistics for incoming staff and their families
* Delivering information sessions and training to HR colleagues and stakeholders across the organisation on immigration changes, compliance, visa sponsorship and policy adherence

**About Us**

Human Resources sits within the portfolio of the Deputy Vice-Chancellor People and Operations, delivering high-level strategic advisory services to Macquarie University and its entities including Macquarie University Hospital and Health Clinics, and U@MQ, the University's commercial enterprise. Our HR Business Partnering teams and Centres of Expertise span Employee Relations, Talent Acquisition, Remuneration, and Capability, Culture and Inclusion, with HR Shared Services and HR Applications underpinning the portfolio.

The Talent Acquisition team is the specialist function responsible for attracting and acquiring domestic and international talent across the University and its entities. Our work is guided by Macquarie's values: collective ambition, purposeful collaboration, bold innovation and genuine care.

**About You (Selection Criteria)**

You are an immigration and mobility specialist who reads legislation closely, keeps meticulous records and explains complex requirements in plain language. You navigate large organisations with ease, handle sensitive personal information with discretion, and find practical solutions when a case does not fit the standard pathway.

  

* Qualifications in HR, business, law or a related discipline and/or substantial relevant experience; OMARA registration desirable
* Demonstrated experience in immigration consulting, corporate mobility or global relocation, ideally within a university, large public sector institution or comparable regulated environment
* Detailed knowledge of Australian immigration legislation and visa processes, including visa subclasses 407, 408, 482 and 186, academic exemptions and pathways relevant to research and higher education
* Proven expertise in employer-sponsored visas, nomination processing and immigration compliance, with the capability to interpret and apply migration legislation autonomously within a complex organisational context
* High-level stakeholder engagement skills, including liaison with government agencies, external legal counsel and senior University stakeholders, along with discretion in handling personal data
* Well-developed case management skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the capacity to organise multiple priorities within tight timelines
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience delivering information sessions or training on compliance-related matters

**How to Apply**

To be considered, please apply online with your CV and a cover letter outlining how your experience aligns with the selection criteria (above).

**We reserve the right to progress or decline an application prior to the application closing date.**

For enquiries, or a confidential conversation about the role please contact Sarah Bate, Head of Talent Acquisition at sarah.bate@mq.edu.au

Macquarie is a university engaged with the real and often complex problems and opportunities that define our lives. Since our foundation over 60 years ago, we have aspired to be a different type of university. Over the years, we have grown to become the centre of a vibrant local and global community. Connect with us today.

We rank amongst the top employers in the Australian Workplace Employers Index. Explore the fantastic benefits available to you when you become part of the team at Macquarie University.

Your employment is conditional upon the completion and maintenance of all role-required pre-employment or background checks in terms satisfactory to the University.

***Help unlock the biology of motor neurone disease and contribute to the search for new treatments***

Motor neurone disease (MND) remains one of the most complex challenges in neuroscience, and the laboratory work behind every discovery matters. As a Research Assistant in the Macquarie University Centre for Motor Neuron Disease, you will work at the bench alongside researchers investigating the cellular mechanisms and molecular pathways of neurodegeneration, and helping to evaluate new treatment strategies in cell and zebrafish models.

You will join a research community of more than 70 people focused on MND, with access to state-of-the-art facilities, advanced imaging and preclinical models, and an active Early Career Researcher network ('EnCouRage'). Reporting to Associate Professor Marco Morsch, you will be part of a team where technical care and curiosity are valued equally, and where your day-to-day contribution feeds directly into research with real human impact.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with hands-on molecular and cellular biology experience who would like to grow their research career within a recognised centre of excellence, with scope to develop new techniques, contribute to publications and build lasting research relationships across the University and beyond.

**About the Role**

Working under the direction of the principal researcher, you will provide practical research and laboratory assistance across a portfolio of MND projects. Your responsibilities will include:

  

* Providing research assistance to projects examining the molecular and cellular mechanisms of neurodegeneration in MND, in line with approved research protocols
* Undertaking and assisting with a range of cellular biology and preclinical research projects, including work in cell and zebrafish models
* Participating in, and assisting with, data management and analysis
* Updating and maintaining databases for project samples and research data
* Contributing to day-to-day laboratory management, including equipment, consumables and record keeping
* Building effective working relationships with a diverse range of researchers, professional staff and students
* Working in line with relevant EEO, WHS, biosafety and research ethics requirements

Please note that work hours may vary from time to time to accommodate operational needs.

**About Us**

Macquarie University's Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences builds on our aspiration to have the nation's first fully integrated Academic Health Sciences Centre under a university's leadership. It brings together the excellent work of medical and allied-health clinicians and researchers across the University and around the country, with unparalleled access to the world-leading clinical resources and research facilities found only on our campus.

The Centre for Motor Neuron Disease is well integrated into the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Human Sciences and the Department of Biomedical Sciences. The Centre has established state-of-the-art research facilities and offers outstanding development options, including an active Early Career Researcher support network ('EnCouRage'), within a team of more than 70 staff working on MND.

**About You**

You are a capable laboratory scientist who enjoys precise, methodical work and takes pride in reliable, well-documented results. You bring practical molecular and cellular biology skills, clear communication, and the organisational habits needed to keep multiple projects moving in a busy research environment.

**Selection Criteria**

* Knowledge and understanding of cell biology, genetic and genomic analysis
* Experience with molecular and cellular biology techniques such as DNA/RNA purification, cell culture, fluorescent microscopy, western blotting and immunostaining
* Experience with molecular biology techniques such as DNA cloning (Gibson, Gateway), DNA construct assembly, PCR, gel electrophoresis and in vitro mRNA production

* Well-organised approach to work, with the ability to prioritise, manage multiple tasks and meet competing deadlines
